news.title: MFA Prompt Bombing: Why Your Second Factor Isn't Saving You
news.description: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) was supposed to close a critical gap in identity security. It meant that, even if an attacker possessed the account credentials, they couldn't log in without the second factor. While that logic was sound, attackers have now figured out that they don't need to steal the second factor: they just need the user to hand it over.   If your workforce authenticates with push-based MFA, this attack is a live threat to your organization today.
